name_zh: 曾子：慎独自省·修齐治平·道统传承
name_en: Zengzi: Shen-Du Watchfulness · Eight Steps · Dao-School Transmission
historical_domains: 伦理学/孝道哲学 / Ethics / Filial Piety Philosophy
心性论/工夫论 / Mind-Nature Theory / Practice Methodology
政治哲学/教化理论 / Political Philosophy / Education Theory
intellectual_tradition: 儒家学派/思孟学派先驱
unique_thinking: 曾子是孔子弟子中唯一将'慎独自省'系统化为工夫论核心方法的儒家思想家；他创建了《大学》八目（格物致知诚意正心修身齐家治国平天下）这一由内而外的完整实践链条；他将孝从家庭伦理提升为本体论原则（'夫孝，德之本也'）；他通过忠恕一贯概括孔子思想精髓；其道统传承（曾申→子思→孟子）成为儒家正统谱系的核心。他是Protreptic中唯一系统整合慎独工夫论、八目实践论、孝道本体论和道统传承理论的思想家。

忠恕一贯法（《论语·里仁》吾道一以贯之）
自省改过法（《论语·学而》日三省吾身）
士人担当法（《论语·泰伯》弘毅任重道远）
临终大节法（《论语·泰伯》启予足启予手；《孝经》身体发肤）
内圣外王贯通法（《论语·泰伯》托孤寄命临大节不可夺；《大学》）
民本教化法（《孝经·三才章》先王见教之可以化民也）
道统传承法（《论语·泰伯》君子所贵乎道者三）

proposed_steps: 第一步：慎独自省——以'君子必慎其独也'为起点，培养独处时的道德自觉和自我监控能力
第二步：忠恕一贯——以'吾道一以贯之，忠恕而已矣'把握孔子思想核心
第三步：三省吾身——通过'日三省吾身'的日常反思机制持续检视忠信习三维度
第四步：修齐治平——以《大学》八目为完整实践路径，从格物致知到治国平天下
第五步：孝道本体——以《孝经》将孝从家庭伦理提升为一切德行的根本和教化起点
第六步：士人担当——以'士不可以不弘毅，任重而道远'确立知识分子的终极使命
第七步：临终大节——以'战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰'的态度贯穿生命全程
第八步：内圣外王——将内在修养与外在事功贯通，在重大关头保持不可动摇的道德定力
第九步：民本教化——以孝道教化为先，实现'不刑而治'的理想社会秩序
第十步：道统传承——自觉承担孔子文化使命，通过思孟学派将儒家道统系统化传递
expected_zh: 确立慎独自省为儒家工夫论的核心方法，影响宋明理学心性修养传统
创建《大学》八目实践体系，为后世提供完整的修己治人方法论
将孝道提升为本体论原则，奠定中国传统社会的核心价值基础
通过忠恕一贯概括孔子思想精髓，为理解儒家学说提供关键钥匙
建立士人担当精神传统，塑造中国知识分子的身份认同和精神品格
expected_en: Established Shen-Du (watchfulness when alone) as the core method of Confucian practice, influencing Song-Ming Neo-Confucian mind-nature cultivation tradition
Created the Great Learning's Eight Steps practical system, providing a complete self-cultivation and governance methodology for later generations
Elevated filial piety to an ontological principle, laying the core value foundation of traditional Chinese society
Summarized Confucius's teaching essence as Zhong-Shu unity, providing the key to understanding Confucian doctrine
Established the scholar-responsibility spirit tradition, shaping the identity and character of Chinese intellectuals
applications: 个人修养与自我管理——运用慎独自省法、自省改过法
领导力发展与组织治理——运用修齐治平法、内圣外王贯通法
家庭伦理与代际关系——运用孝道本体法、民本教化法
知识分子的使命担当——运用士人担当法、道统传承法
组织文化与伦理建设——运用忠恕一贯法、民本教化法

distinctiveness.vs_kongzi: 孔子重'仁'的普遍性（己所不欲勿施于人），曾子更重'慎独'的内化工夫；孔子以'正名'为政治起点，曾子以'修齐治平八目'为实践路径。
distinctiveness.vs_mengzi: 孟子重'性善论'与'四端说'（恻隐羞恶辞让是非），曾子重'慎独自省'的工夫实践；孟子从人性论出发论证善，曾子从修养论出发构建工夫。
distinctiveness.vs_xunzi: 荀子重'性恶论'与'化性起伪'的外在规范，曾子重'慎独自省'的内在自觉；荀子强调礼法的外在约束，曾子强调诚意的内化自律。
distinctiveness.vs_zisi: 子思（孔伋）重'天命之谓性'的形上建构，曾子重'慎独自省'的实践工夫；子思偏哲学本体论，曾子偏实践方法论。

caveats: '慎独'的工夫论依赖于对内在道德自觉的高度信任，缺乏外在制衡机制
'八目'的由内而外路径假设内在修养必然导致外在事功，忽略了制度环境的制约
'孝道本体化'将家庭伦理推广为政治原则，可能导致公私领域的混淆
'忠恕一贯'的概括虽简洁但可能简化了孔子思想的复杂性

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『君子必慎其独也』——《大学》诚意章与《中庸》首章共同申明的工夫：在无人监督的独处之境（朱熹所谓『人所不知而己独知』之地）仍保持道德自觉，不自欺、不欺隐。慎独把外在规范内化为自我要求，专在『隐』『微』处用力，是人前慎行的根基；曾子一系以之作为修身工夫的起点。（按：慎独非曾子一系专用术语，《荀子·不苟》与马王堆帛书《五行》皆言慎独。）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'The gentleman must be watchful over himself when alone.' A practice jointly affirmed by the Great Learning (chapter on making the will sincere) and the Doctrine of the Mean (ch. 1): keeping moral awareness in solitude — where no one watches but oneself alone knows — neither self-deceiving nor concealing. Shen-du internalizes external norms and works precisely at the hidden and the minute; the Zengzi line takes it as the entry practice of self-cultivation. (Note: shen-du is not exclusive to the Zengzi line — the Xunzi and the silk-manuscript Wuxing also discuss it.)
process_zh: 培养独处时的自我觉察能力
在无人监督时检查内心念头的纯正性（毋自欺）
将外在规范完全内化为自我要求
在独处中保持甚至加强道德自律
process_en: Cultivate the capacity for self-awareness in solitude
Check, when no one is watching, whether one's inner intentions are pure (wu-zi-qi: not deceiving oneself)
Fully internalize external norms as one's own demands
Sustain and even strengthen moral self-discipline when alone
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 此谓诚于中，形于外，故君子必慎其独也。（《大学》）／莫见乎隐，莫显乎微，故君子慎其独也。（《中庸》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'This is what is meant by sincerity within giving form without: the gentleman must be watchful over himself when alone.' (Great Learning) / 'Nothing is more visible than the hidden, nothing more manifest than the minute: therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.' (Doctrine of the Mean)
representative_cases_zh: 《大学》诚意章以『诚于中，形于外』说明内心真实必显露于外，紧接『故君子必慎其独也』——诚意与慎独是一体两面（原文既定稿核验）
《中庸》首章以『莫见乎隐，莫显乎微』指出隐蔽细微之处最见心术，故君子在独处时尤须谨慎；定稿已移除旧稿混入的后世成语『不欺暗室』并标注留证
representative_cases_en: The Great Learning's chapter on sincerity: 'sincerity within gives form without' — what is truly in the mind always shows; it concludes 'therefore the gentleman must be watchful over himself when alone': sincerity and shen-du are two sides of one practice

The Doctrine of the Mean's opening chapter: 'nothing is more visible than the hidden, nothing more manifest than the minute' — hence the gentleman is especially careful alone; the later idiom 'not deceiving in a dark room' was removed and documented
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 《大学》《中庸》传统上系于曾子一系：朱熹《大学章句》称『经一章，盖孔子之言，而曾子述之；其传十章，则曾子之意而门人记之也』；《中庸》依《史记·孔子世家》系于孔子之孙孔伋（子思）。但两篇的作者与成书年代今有争议（《大学》本为《礼记》第四十二篇，现代学者多定为战国晚期之作），故『慎独工夫＝曾子』属唐宋以来传统归属，非先秦实证定论。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: The Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean are traditionally tied to the Zengzi line (Zhu Xi's Great Learning commentary: 'the classic chapter is the words of Confucius as narrated by Zengzi; the ten commentaries are Zengzi's meaning recorded by his disciples'; the Doctrine of the Mean is attributed by the Shiji to Confucius's grandson Kong Ji/Zisi). Yet the authorship and date of both are disputed in modern scholarship (the Great Learning was ch. 42 of the Liji, now usually dated to the late Warring States), so 'shen-du = Zengzi' is a traditional attribution, not an empirically settled fact.

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『古之欲明明德于天下者，先治其国……』《大学》提出三纲领（明明德、亲民、止于至善）与八条目（格物、致知、诚意、正心、修身、齐家、治国、平天下），构成由内而外、由个体到天下的完整实践链条，是儒家『修己治人』工夫的系统化表达，也是中国古代影响最大的政治—伦理实践方法论。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'The ancients who wished to illustrate illustrious virtue throughout the world first ordered well their states…' The Great Learning sets out the Three Guidelines (illustrating virtue, renewing the people, resting in the highest good) and the Eight Steps (investigating things, extending knowledge, sincere will, rectified mind, cultivated self, regulated family, governed state, peaceful world), forming a complete practical chain from the inner self to the world — ancient China's most influential political-ethical methodology of self-cultivation and governance.
process_zh: 格物：探究事物原理以获得真知
致知：扩展认知至全面理解
诚意：使意念真诚不欺
正心：端正内心不受情绪干扰
修身：完善个人品德修养
齐家：管理好家庭家族
治国：治理国家社会
平天下：实现天下太平
process_en: Ge-wu: investigate the principles of things to gain true knowledge
Zhi-zhi: extend knowledge to comprehensive understanding
Cheng-yi: make the will sincere and undeceived
Zheng-xin: rectify the mind so it is not disturbed by emotion
Xiu-shen: perfect one's personal character
Qi-jia: order one's family and household
Zhi-guo: govern the state and society
Ping-tianxia: bring peace to the world
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 古之欲明明德于天下者，先治其国；欲治其国者，先齐其家；欲齐其家者，先修其身；欲修其身者，先正其心；欲正其心者，先诚其意；欲诚其意者，先致其知；致知在格物。（《大学》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'The ancients who wished to illustrate illustrious virtue throughout the world first ordered well their states; wishing to order well their states, they first regulated their families; wishing to regulate their families, they first cultivated themselves; wishing to cultivate themselves, they first rectified their minds; wishing to rectify their minds, they first made their wills sincere; wishing to make their wills sincere, they first extended their knowledge; the extension of knowledge lies in the investigation of things.' (Great Learning)
representative_cases_zh: 《大学》经文以八条目排成先后相因的阶梯：格物→致知→诚意→正心→修身→齐家→治国→平天下，并以『物有本末，事有终始』点明本末次序（引文逐字核验）
三纲领（明明德、亲民、止于至善）与八条目相互支撑：纲领定方向，条目定次第。定稿补全『三纲领＋八条目』表述，并标注『内圣外王』语出《庄子·天下篇》而非儒家原语
representative_cases_en: The Great Learning's classic text arranges the eight steps as a dependent ladder — ge-wu, zhi-zhi, cheng-yi, zheng-xin, xiu-shen, qi-jia, zhi-guo, ping-tianxia — noting that 'things have root and branch, affairs have end and beginning' (quote verified)

The three guidelines (manifest virtue, renew the people, rest in the highest good) and eight steps support each other: guidelines set direction, steps set order. The final text restored the 'three guidelines + eight steps' formulation and noted that 'inner sage, outer king' comes from Zhuangzi, not the Confucian canon
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 文本归属争议同 M-ZX-001（《大学》作者系于曾子的说法本于二程—朱熹一系）。又：概括语『内圣外王』语出《庄子·天下篇》『是故内圣外王之道，闇而不明，郁而不发』，非儒家原语，属后世（尤其宋明理学）对儒家修养—事功结构的概括，使用时宜标注来源。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: Textual attribution is as disputed as in M-ZX-001 (the Zengzi authorship claim stems from the Cheng-Zhu tradition). Note also that the summarizing phrase 'inner sage, outer king' comes from the Zhuangzi (Tian Xia chapter), not from the Confucian corpus — it is a later (especially Song-Ming Neo-Confucian) shorthand.

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.domain_en: Philosophy of Filial Piety / Ethical Foundations
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『夫孝，德之本也，教之所由生也』——《孝经》径将孝推为一切德行的根本与教化的起点，认为忠、义、礼等德目皆可自孝道推衍（『移孝作忠』『天经地义』）。《大戴礼记·曾子大孝》更称『夫孝者，天下之大经也』『身者，亲之遗体也』，把孝由家庭伦理提升为贯通天人、连接个体与政治秩序的普遍原则——这是曾子一系对中国伦理—政治思想最具穿透力的贡献之一。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'Filial piety is the root of all virtue, and the source from which all moral teaching springs.' The Classic of Filial Piety raises filial piety to the root of the virtues and the origin of moral teaching, from which loyalty, righteousness and propriety may be extended ('transferring filial service into loyalty'; 'the constant of heaven and righteousness of earth'). The Da Dai Liji (Zengzi on Great Filial Piety) goes further: 'filial piety is the great constant of the world'; 'the body is the legacy of one's parents.' Family ethics is thereby elevated into a universal principle linking heaven, the individual and political order — one of the Zengzi line's most penetrating contributions.
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.source_chapter: 《孝经·开宗明义章》；《大戴礼记·曾子大孝》
process_zh: 认识孝道是一切德行的根本来源
将孝敬父母的情感推广至对师长、社会的责任
在政治领域中实现『移孝作忠』
以孝道为基点构建完整的道德秩序
process_en: Recognize filial piety as the root source of all virtues
Extend the affection of serving parents to teachers and society at large
Translate filial devotion into civic loyalty in public life ('moving filial piety to loyalty')
Build a complete moral order on the foundation of filial piety
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 夫孝，德之本也，教之所由生也。（《孝经·开宗明义章》）／夫孝者，天下之大经也。（《大戴礼记·曾子大孝》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'Filial piety is the root of all virtue and the source of all moral teaching.' (Classic of Filial Piety, ch. 1) / 'Filial piety is the great constant of the world.' (Da Dai Liji, Zengzi on Great Filial Piety)
representative_cases_zh: 《史记·仲尼弟子列传》载『孔子以为能通孝道，故授之业，作孝经』——曾子被传统视为《孝经》一系的传述者（归属争议已标注，不作实证断言）
《大戴礼记·曾子大孝》以『孝有三：大孝尊亲，其次不辱，其下能养』『夫孝者，天下之大经也』分孝为三等并上升为天下大经；定稿新增该篇原文比证，补强曾子文献依据
representative_cases_en: The Shiji records that 'Confucius, considering him able to understand filial piety, gave him the teaching and composed the Classic of Filial Piety' — Zengzi is traditionally seen as its transmitter (attribution flagged as traditional, not asserted as fact)

The Da Dai Liji's 'Zengzi on Great Filial Piety' grades filial piety ('the greatest honors parents, next does not disgrace them, the least merely supports them') and calls it 'the great constant of the world'; the final text added this textual comparison to strengthen Zengzi's documentary basis
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 《孝经》开宗明义章为孔子答曾子之问（『仲尼居，曾子侍』），传统以《孝经》归曾子：《史记·仲尼弟子列传》载『孔子以为能通孝道，故授之业，作孝经』，《汉书·艺文志》称『《孝经》者，孔子为曾子陈孝道也』；但今本《孝经》的成书与作者（战国末至汉初说）今有争议。『移孝作忠』出《孝经·广扬名章》，『天经地义』出《孝经·三才章》，皆经文而非曾子自撰之语。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: The opening chapter of the Classic of Filial Piety records Confucius answering Zengzi; the book is traditionally ascribed to Zengzi (Shiji: 'Confucius, judging him able to master filial piety, imparted the tradition to him — he made the Classic of Filial Piety'; Hanshu Yiwenzhi: 'the Classic of Filial Piety is Confucius setting forth filial piety for Zengzi'). Modern scholarship, however, dates its composition to the late Warring States or early Han. 'Transferring filial service into loyalty' and 'the constant of heaven and righteousness of earth' are scripture phrases, not Zengzi's own words.

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『吾道一以贯之』——孔子以此语授曾子，曾子以『忠恕而已矣』一言概括之：忠是尽己之心（正己），恕是推己及人（达人），二者一体两面，构成儒家伦理实践的一贯之道，也为理解孔子思想体系提供了最简洁的钥匙。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'My Way is bound together with one thread': Confucius gave this teaching to Zengzi, who summed it up as 'loyalty and reciprocity alone.' Zhong (loyalty) is fulfilling one's own heart; shu (reciprocity) is extending oneself to others. Two sides of one body, together they form the consistent way of Confucian ethical practice — the simplest key to the Master's thought.
process_zh: 以忠道尽己之心，做到真诚无欺
以恕道推己及人，理解包容他人
在忠与恕的辩证统一中把握儒家核心精神
将一贯之道贯彻于一切伦理实践中
process_en: Practice loyalty (zhong) by fully exerting one's own heart with sincerity
Practice reciprocity (shu) by extending oneself to others with understanding
Grasp the Confucian core in the dialectical unity of zhong and shu
Carry the single thread through all ethical practice
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 子曰：『参乎！吾道一以贯之。』曾子曰：『唯。』子出，门人问曰：『何谓也？』曾子曰：『夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。』（《论语·里仁》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'Shen, my Way is bound together with one thread.' The Master went out, and the other disciples asked, 'What does he mean?' Zengzi said, 'The Master's Way is nothing but loyalty and reciprocity.' (Analects, Li Ren)
representative_cases_zh: 《论语·里仁》记孔子呼『参乎！吾道一以贯之』，曾子答『唯』；出而告门人『夫子之道，忠恕而已矣』——一问一答间以忠恕两点概括一贯之道（含对话全段核验）
『尽己之谓忠，推己之谓恕』（朱熹《论语集注》）为宋代注疏的经典界定；定稿已将该句标注为注疏语，不与曾子原语混同
representative_cases_en: In the Analects (Li Ren) Confucius calls, 'Shen, my Way is one thread running through it'; Zengzi answers 'Yes'; questioned by the disciples he explains, 'the Master's Way is simply loyalty and reciprocity' — the whole dialogue verified

'Exerting oneself to the utmost is zhong; extending oneself to others is shu' (Zhu Xi's Collected Commentaries) is the classic Song-dynasty gloss; the final text flags it as commentary language, not Zengzi's own words
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 定义中『忠＝尽己之心、恕＝推己及人』的训释本于朱熹《论语集注》『尽己之谓忠，推己之谓恕』（并见《中庸》『忠恕违道不远，施诸己而不愿，亦勿施于人』），属宋代注疏语，非先秦原文，此处按注疏惯例标明。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: The gloss 'loyalty = fulfilling one's own heart; reciprocity = extending oneself to others' follows Zhu Xi's Analects commentary ('fulfilling oneself is called zhong; extending oneself is called shu'), a Song-dynasty gloss rather than pre-Qin wording; it is flagged here as commentary.

在忠与恕的辩证统一中把握儒家核心精神

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『吾日三省吾身』——曾子创立的制度化自省方法：每日从忠（为人谋是否尽心）、信（与朋友交是否诚信）、习（所传之学是否躬行）三个维度检视自身，发现偏差即行纠正，把道德修养从偶然的顿悟转化为日常的习惯性训练，是儒家修身工夫的核心机制。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'Each day I examine myself on three counts': the systematic self-examination Zengzi instituted — checking daily three dimensions: loyalty (in serving others), trustworthiness (with friends), and practice (whether what was passed on is practiced). Deviations are corrected as found, turning moral cultivation from occasional insight into daily habit: the core mechanism of Confucian self-cultivation.
process_zh: 建立日常自省的习惯和框架
从忠（对人）、信（交友）、习（学问）三个维度检视自身
发现偏差后及时纠正并调整行为
通过持续自省实现道德境界的阶梯式提升
process_en: Establish a daily habit and framework of self-examination
Examine oneself on three counts: loyalty in serving others, trustworthiness with friends, practice of what one teaches
Correct deviations promptly and adjust behavior
Climb the ladder of moral cultivation through sustained self-reflection
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 曾子曰：『吾日三省吾身：为人谋而不忠乎？与朋友交而不信乎？传不习乎？』（《论语·学而》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'Each day I examine myself on three counts: in planning for others, have I been unfaithful? In intercourse with friends, have I been untrustworthy? Have I failed to practice what was passed down to me?' (Analects, Xue Er)
representative_cases_zh: 《论语·学而》曾子自述『吾日三省吾身：为人谋而不忠乎？与朋友交而不信乎？传不习乎？』——把自省固定为每日三问的例行功课（引文逐字核验，无归属争议）
『三省』旧注有两解：朱熹《集注》以忠、信、习『三事』解（与曾子三问相应），另一解为『三次』；定稿从『三事』说并在 verification.note 记录
representative_cases_en: In the Analects (Xue Er) Zengzi says, 'I examine myself daily on three points: in serving others, have I been unfaithful? In dealings with friends, have I been untrustworthy? Have I practiced what I was taught?' — reflection fixed as a daily routine (quote verified)

'Three examinations' has two readings: Zhu Xi's commentary takes three matters (loyalty, trust, practice), matching Zengzi's three questions; the other reading is 'three times.' The final text follows the 'three matters' reading and records the alternative
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 无归属争议：《论语·学而》该章明文系于曾子（『曾子曰』），非转述、非后人推定。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: No attribution dispute: the Xue Er chapter explicitly attributes the saying to Zengzi ('Zengzi said'), directly and not by later inference.

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『士不可以不弘毅，任重而道远』——曾子将士人的道德担当提升到极致：以推行仁道为终身使命，生命终结方可止息。这种把个人命运与天下大道紧扣的担当精神，成为后世士大夫的精神支柱与身份认同来源。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'A scholar cannot be without breadth of mind and vigorous endurance: his burden is heavy and his course is long.' Zengzi raised the scholar's moral charge to its utmost — making the promotion of humaneness a lifelong mission that ends only with death. This identification of personal destiny with the Way became the spiritual mainstay of later Chinese scholar-officials.
process_zh: 确立以天下道义为个人使命的宏大志向
认识责任的重大和道路的长远
在困境中坚持道义担当不后退
将个人价值与社会责任融为一体
process_en: Set a grand aspiration making the Way one's personal mission
Recognize the weight of the burden and the length of the road
Hold to one's ethical commitment without retreat under hardship
Fuse personal worth with social responsibility
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 曾子曰：『士不可以不弘毅，任重而道远。仁以为己任，不亦重乎？死而后已，不亦远乎？』（《论语·泰伯》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'A scholar cannot be without breadth and resoluteness; his burden is heavy and his course long. Making humaneness his burden — is it not heavy? Ceasing only at death — is it not long?' (Analects, Tai Bo)
representative_cases_zh: 《论语·泰伯》『士不可以不弘毅，任重而道远。仁以为己任，不亦重乎？死而后已，不亦远乎？』——以终身践行仁道界定士的使命（引文逐字核验，无归属争议）
该章以『任重』对应『仁以为己任』、以『道远』对应『死而后已』，把责任与时间尺度一并立为标准，成为后世士人精神认同的经典出处
representative_cases_en: Analects (Tai Bo): 'The scholar cannot but be strong and resolute, for his burden is heavy and his road is long. To take humaneness as one's own burden — is it not heavy? To end only with death — is it not long?' — the scholar's mission defined by lifelong practice of ren (quote verified)

The chapter maps 'heavy burden' to 'taking ren as one's own' and 'long road' to 'ending only with death,' setting both weight and time-scale as the standard — a classic locus of scholar-official identity
modern_applications_zh: 公共知识分子角色定位
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 无归属争议：《论语·泰伯》该章明文系于曾子（『曾子曰』）。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: No attribution dispute: the Tai Bo chapter explicitly attributes the saying to Zengzi ('Zengzi said').

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『启予足，启予手』——曾子临终命弟子检视手足，以《诗》『战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰』自述一生守身之慎，以身体发肤的完好作为一生践行孝道的最终验证：『身体发肤，受之父母，不敢毁伤，孝之始也』（《孝经》）。将生命最后一刻的道德完整性视为最高价值，体现儒家对道德完整与人格尊严的极致追求（曾子易箦之事，见《礼记·檀弓上》，则为临终守礼的另一证例）。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'Open my feet; open my hands.' On his deathbed Zengzi had his disciples inspect his body, quoting the Odes ('trembling and fearful, as if on the brink of a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice') to describe a lifetime of careful keeping — the intactness of body and hair being the final proof of a life of filial piety ('the body, hair and skin are received from parents; not daring to injure them is the beginning of filial piety'). To treat moral integrity at the very end as the highest value is the Confucian pursuit of completeness and dignity in extremis. (Zengzi's changing of his mat, recorded in the Liji, Tan Gong, offers a further example of ritual care at death.)
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.source_chapter: 《论语·泰伯》；《孝经·开宗明义章》；补充：《礼记·檀弓上》
process_zh: 将生命全程视为对道德责任的践行
在生命的每个阶段保持谨慎敬畏的态度
以最终的道德完整性为人生画上句号
将『不敢毁伤』扩展为对一切道德承诺的坚守
process_en: Treat the whole of life as the practice of a moral commitment
Keep a cautious, reverent attitude at every stage of life
Close one's life with final moral integrity intact
Extend 'not daring to injure' to every moral pledge
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 曾子有疾，召门弟子曰：『启予足！启予手！《诗》云：战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰。而今而后，吾知免夫！小子！』（《论语·泰伯》）／身体发肤，受之父母，不敢毁伤，孝之始也。（《孝经·开宗明义章》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'Zengzi being ill, he called his disciples: Open my feet; open my hands. The Odes say: Trembling and fearful, as if on the brink of a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice. From now on I know I am spared, my children!' (Analects, Tai Bo) / 'Our bodies — to every hair and bit of skin — are received from our parents, and we must not presume to injure them: this is the beginning of filial piety.' (Classic of Filial Piety, ch. 1)
representative_cases_zh: 《论语·泰伯》曾子临终召门弟子『启予足！启予手！』并引《诗》『战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰』，以守身完好自证一生谨慎（引文逐字核验）
《礼记·檀弓上》『曾子易箦』：临终坚持换掉不合礼制的席子，守礼至最后一刻；定稿将出处补全为《论语·泰伯》＋《孝经·开宗明义章》并补此证例
representative_cases_en: Analects (Tai Bo): on his deathbed Zengzi has his disciples inspect his hands and feet, quoting the Odes — 'trembling with caution, as if on the brink of a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice' — proving a lifetime's care (quote verified)

The Liji (Tangong I) tells 'Zengzi changes his mat': dying, he insists on replacing a mat that does not accord with ritual, keeping propriety to the last moment; the final text completed the sources (Analects, Classic of Filial Piety) and added this example
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 『身体发肤，受之父母』为《孝经·开宗明义章》孔子告曾子之语，其归属争议同 M-ZX-003；『曾子易箦』见《礼记·檀弓上》，属后出记载，仅作补充例证。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: 'Body, hair and skin received from parents' are words of Confucius to Zengzi in the Classic of Filial Piety (attribution disputed as in M-ZX-003); the 'changing of the mat' story is recorded in the Liji, Tan Gong, and is used here only as supplementary evidence.

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.name_en: Inner Sage Outer King Integration Method
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.domain_en: Inner Sage & Outer King / Political Philosophy
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『可以托六尺之孤，可以寄百里之命，临大节而不可夺也』——曾子以此界定真正的君子：在重大关头怀抱不可动摇的道德定力。此条把内在修养（诚意正心）与外在事功（治国平天下）贯通为一，是《大学》八目结构的人格化表达，也是后世儒家政治哲学的核心范式。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'One who can be entrusted with the orphan of a young state, whose authority can be trusted with the command of a hundred li, whose character cannot be shaken when facing great crises' — Zengzi's definition of the true gentleman: unshakable moral firmness at the decisive moment. The mode binds inner cultivation (sincere will, rectified mind) to outer achievement (governing the state, pacifying the world): the Eight Steps of the Great Learning rendered as character, and a core paradigm of later Confucian political philosophy.
process_zh: 通过内省修养建立不可动摇的道德根基
将内在德性转化为外在治理能力
在重大危机和抉择面前保持道义定力
通过传承将个人修养扩展为制度化的教化体系
process_en: Build an unshakable moral foundation through inner cultivation
Convert inner virtue into the capacity for outward governance
Keep ethical resolve at moments of great crisis and choice
Extend personal cultivation into institutionalized edification through transmission
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 曾子曰：『可以托六尺之孤，可以寄百里之命，临大节而不可夺也。君子人与？君子人也。』（《论语·泰伯》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'One who can be entrusted with the orphan of a young state, whose authority can be trusted with the command of a hundred li — when facing great crises his character cannot be shaken. Is he a gentleman? He is a gentleman.' (Analects, Tai Bo)
representative_cases_zh: 《论语·泰伯》曾子以『可以托六尺之孤，可以寄百里之命，临大节而不可夺也』界定君子——大节关头不可夺其志（引文逐字核验）
《大学》八目把诚意正心（内）与治国平天下（外）连为一条路径，此条即其人格化表达；定稿已标注『内圣外王』语出《庄子·天下篇》，属后世概括
representative_cases_en: Analects (Tai Bo): Zengzi defines the gentleman as one 'to whom one can entrust an orphan of six cubits, and the command of a hundred li, whom no great crisis can shake' (quote verified)

The Great Learning's eight steps link sincerity and rectified mind (inner) with governing the state and pacifying the world (outer); this mode personifies that structure. The final text notes that 'inner sage, outer king' comes from Zhuangzi and is a later summary
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 术语注意：『内圣外王』语出《庄子·天下篇》『是故内圣外王之道，闇而不明，郁而不发』，非曾子原语，亦非先秦儒家自用语汇，系后世（尤其宋明理学）对儒家修养—事功结构的概括；本条以之命名而须标注来源，避免误植为曾子原创术语。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: Terminological note: 'inner sage, outer king' comes from the Zhuangzi (Tian Xia): 'Thus the way of the inner sage and outer king was obscured and not illuminated.' It is neither Zengzi's phrase nor native Confucian vocabulary, but a later (especially Neo-Confucian) shorthand; the name is retained but its provenance is flagged.

legacy_field_aliases.modern_applications: 同 modern_applications_zh，兼容父卡验收脚本口径

process: 通过内省修养建立不可动摇的道德根基
将内在德性转化为外在治理能力
在重大危机和抉择面前保持道义定力
通过传承将个人修养扩展为制度化的教化体系

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『先王见教之可以化民也』——《孝经·三才章》载孔子之言：古之圣王以博爱、德义、敬让、礼乐、好恶五事为先导，以教化而非刑威化民成俗，故『其教不肃而成，其政不严而治』。此条将家庭伦理（孝）推广为社会政治秩序的基础，以道德教化置于刑罚之前，是儒家『以德治国』的经典表述（曾子一系所传《孝经》为其文献载体）。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'The former kings saw that teaching could transform the people' — words of Confucius recorded in the Classic of Filial Piety (ch. 3, 'Three Powers'): the ancient kings led with love, righteousness, deference, ritual and music, and clear likes and dislikes; transformation came by teaching rather than by punishment, so that 'their teaching was accomplished without severity, their government ordered without harshness.' Family ethics (filial piety) is extended into the basis of social and political order — the classic statement of Confucian 'rule by virtue,' carried in the Classic of Filial Piety transmitted by the Zengzi line.
process_zh: 将道德教化置于刑罚之前作为首要治理手段
通过孝道建立社会伦理基础
以榜样示范引导民风转变
在教化中实现自愿的社会秩序
process_en: Put moral edification before punishment as the primary means of governance
Build a social ethical foundation through filial piety
Guide popular custom by exemplary leadership
Achieve voluntary social order through edification
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 子曰：『……先王见教之可以化民也，是故先之以博爱，而民莫遗其亲；陈之以德义，而民兴行；先之以敬让，而民不争；导之以礼乐，而民和睦；示之以好恶，而民知禁。』（《孝经·三才章》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: '…The former kings saw that teaching could transform the people: therefore they set love first, and none neglected their parents; they set forth righteousness, and the people rose to practice it; they set deference first, and the people did not contend; they guided with ritual and music, and the people were harmonious; they showed what to love and hate, and the people knew their prohibitions.' (Classic of Filial Piety, ch. 3)
representative_cases_zh: 《孝经·三才章》载孔子答曾子『甚哉，孝之大也』之问：『先王见教之可以化民也，是故先之以博爱……示之以好恶，而民知禁』——以五事为先导，教成而政治（定稿替换旧伪句后逐字核验）
同章『其教不肃而成，其政不严而治』二句为原文表述（定稿据此改写定义与关键概念，废去今人概括『不刑而治』；旧伪句已作废并留证）
representative_cases_en: Classic of Filial Piety (San Cai): answering Zengzi's question 'how great is filial piety,' Confucius says the ancient kings saw that teaching could transform the people and led with universal love ... and 'showed them likes and dislikes, and the people knew their prohibitions' (verified after replacing a fabricated sentence)

The same chapter's 'its teaching succeeds without severity, its government rules without harshness' is the original wording on which the final text rewrote the definition and key concepts; the old fabricated sentence is voided and documented
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 引文出自《孝经·三才章》孔子之言（曾子问『甚哉，孝之大也』而孔子答），《孝经》归属争议同 M-ZX-003。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: The quotation is Confucius's answer to Zengzi in the Classic of Filial Piety; attribution of the book as a whole is disputed as in M-ZX-003.

通过孝道建立社会伦理基础
以榜样示范引导民风转变
在教化中实现自愿的社会秩序
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.correction_zh: 重大修正：旧稿引文『君子所乎民者，则民亦如是乎』遍检《孝经》全文及先秦文献无此句（联网整句检索 0 命中），判定为伪造/讹变引文，已替换为《孝经·三才章》原文；出处由笼统『《孝经》』精确至『《孝经·三才章》』；『不刑而治』系今人概括，原文作『其教不肃而成，其政不严而治』，定义与关键概念已按原文改写。

thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_zh: 『君子所贵乎道者三』——曾子临终对孟敬子的告诫：动容貌、正颜色、出辞气三事，是君子守道之要（『鸟之将死，其鸣也哀；人之将死，其言也善』）。此条概括曾子作为孔门『传道者』的角色：不仅忠实承受孔子之教（『吾道一以贯之』），且以可传授的工夫与临终的教言把斯文托付后学；后世（唐宋以来）以『孔子—曾子—子思—孟子』为道统谱系，曾子居承上启下之枢。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.definition_en: 'There are three things the gentleman values in the Way' — Zengzi's deathbed charge to Meng Jingzi: composure of demeanor, sincerity of countenance, and care of speech and tone ('when a bird is about to die, its song is mournful; when a man is about to die, his words are good'). The mode captures Zengzi as the Confucian tradition's transmitter: faithfully receiving the Master's teaching ('my Way is one thread') and handing the cultural heritage on through transmissible practice and a final charge. From Tang-Song times the lineage 'Confucius–Zengzi–Zisi–Mencius' was enshrined as the orthodox transmission, with Zengzi as its hinge.
process_zh: 准确理解并概括核心思想精髓
建立可传承的教学体系和工夫论框架
通过弟子一代代传递道统血脉
在传承中保持核心精神的纯正性
process_en: Accurately grasp and summarize the essence of core thought
Build a transmissible teaching system and framework of practice
Pass the lineage on through generations of disciples
Preserve the purity of the core spirit in transmission
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_zh: 曾子有疾，孟敬子问之。曾子言曰：『鸟之将死，其鸣也哀；人之将死，其言也善。君子所贵乎道者三：动容貌，斯远暴慢矣；正颜色，斯近信矣；出辞气，斯远鄙倍矣。笾豆之事，则有司存。』（《论语·泰伯》）
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.key_quote_en: 'Zengzi being ill, Meng Jingzi came to ask after him. Zengzi said: When a bird is about to die, its song is mournful; when a man is about to die, his words are good. There are three things the gentleman values in the Way: in demeanor, to keep far from violence and arrogance; in countenance, to keep near to sincerity; in speech and tone, to keep far from meanness and perversity. As for the sacrificial vessels, there are officers for those.' (Analects, Tai Bo)
representative_cases_zh: 《论语·泰伯》曾子临终告孟敬子『君子所贵乎道者三：动容貌、正颜色、出辞气』——以可传授的工夫与临终教言把斯文托付后学（定稿替换旧误引《子罕》章孔子语）
后世以『孔子—曾子—子思—孟子』为道统谱系（韩愈《原道》首倡、朱熹《中庸章句序》定型）；可考者为《史记》载孔子之孙孔伋（子思）与孟子『受业子思之门人』，曾子与子思的直接师承为后世推定，已作归属标注
representative_cases_en: Analects (Tai Bo): dying, Zengzi charges Meng Jingzi that 'the gentleman values three things in the Way: demeanor, countenance, and speech' — entrusting the tradition through transmissible practice and last words (replacing an earlier misattributed quote from Confucius in the Zi Han chapter)

Later ages formed the lineage 'Confucius-Zengzi-Zisi-Mencius' (initiated by Han Yu's Yuan Dao, fixed by Zhu Xi's preface to the Doctrine of the Mean); documented facts are the Shiji's record of Confucius's grandson Kong Ji (Zisi) and that Mencius 'studied under Zisi's disciples' — a direct Zengzi-to-Zisi link is a later inference and is flagged as such
modern_applications_zh: 知识传承与教育体系设计
学术传统的延续与创新
modern_applications_en: Knowledge transmission and education system design
Continuity and innovation of scholarly traditions
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_zh: 『道统』为唐宋建构的概念（韩愈《原道》首倡、朱熹《中庸章句序》定型），『孔子—曾子—子思—孟子』谱系属该叙事：可考者为《史记·孔子世家》载孔子之孙孔伋（子思），《史记·孟子荀卿列传》载孟子『受业子思之门人』（非亲授）；曾子与子思的直接师承为后世推定，本卡不作实证断言。
thinking_modes_v6_phase20.attribution_note_en: 'Dao-tong' (the orthodox transmission) is a Tang-Song construct (Han Yu's Yuan Dao; Zhu Xi's preface to the Doctrine of the Mean). What is documented: the Shiji records Confucius's grandson Kong Ji (Zisi) and that Mencius 'studied under the disciples of Zisi' (not directly); a direct Zengzi-to-Zisi master-disciple link is a later inference and is not asserted here as fact.
